compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

The project routing overlay (`.rebar/criteria_routing.json`, `code_review` section) can today only define standalone `project.*` criteria; it cannot extend a BUILT-IN overlay's triggers. `registry.glob_triggered_overlays` (src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py:256) reads only the committed routing via `applies_to_globs` (registry.py:236), and `registry.content_triggered_overlays` (registry.py:321) is hardcoded to the deletion-impact removed-declaration regex. The parent epic's two-layer trigger design (committed high-precision tier / project noisy tier) requires a project to be able to add trigger vocabulary to a built-in overlay — starting with `concurrency`, but the mechanism is overlay-id-agnostic (a project could equally add tokens to `performance`).

## Approach

Extend the `code_review` side of the project overlay so an entry keyed by a BUILT-IN overlay id (a member of `OVERLAY_IDS`, registry.py:38) may carry two additive keys: `trigger_tokens` — a list of literal substrings matched case-sensitively against the added and removed lines of the unified diff (file headers `+++`/`---` excluded) — and `applies_to` globs, unioned with the committed globs. Consume both through `registry.effective_routing(repo_root)` (registry.py:173) inside `glob_triggered_overlays` and `content_triggered_overlays`, threading `repo_root` from the single call site `workflow_ops.overlay_union` (src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py:98-99). Positive rationale: this mirrors the plan-review side's proven project trigger mechanism (`trigger.text_all` on `project.engine-layer-enforcement` in this repo's `.rebar/criteria_routing.json`), and literal substrings — not regex — keep the gate a simple filter that is cheap to author and impossible to catastrophically misparse, matching the trigger's filter-not-finder role. ADR 0074 semantics are preserved: for `project.*` ids, empty `applies_to` still means ungated (`project_criterion_applies`, registry.py:282); for built-in ids the project keys are an additive union, so with no project entry present both functions behave exactly as today (committed `applies_to` empty still means escalation-only).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py` — token-matching helper; `effective_routing` consumption in both trigger functions.
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py` — thread `repo_root` into the trigger calls in `overlay_union`.
- `tests/unit/test_criteria_overlay.py` — new cases (this module already covers the project routing overlay).

Documentation of the mechanism is delivered by the sibling dogfood story (it documents mechanism and worked example together).

## Testing

Unit tier (pure in-process functions plus a `tmp_path` repo fixture writing a project `.rebar/criteria_routing.json`; no live boundary, so one tier lower does not exist). Oracle: the returned overlay-id lists.

- Happy path: a project entry on a built-in overlay id with `trigger_tokens: ["FROBNICATE("]` causes `content_triggered_overlays` to return that id for a diff whose added line contains the token.
- Removed-line path: the same token on a removed (`-`) line also fires.
- Glob union: project `applies_to` globs on a built-in id fire `glob_triggered_overlays` for a matching changed file that the committed globs do not match.
- Negative control: with no project overlay present, both functions return their current results (the existing test corpus passes unmodified).
- Malformed input: a non-list `trigger_tokens`, a non-string token, or an entry under an unknown id is ignored without raising.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A tmp project overlay declaring `trigger_tokens` on a built-in overlay id causes `content_triggered_overlays` to return that id for a diff containing the token on an added OR removed line; checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_criteria_overlay.py`.
- [ ] Project `applies_to` globs on a built-in id union with the committed globs in `glob_triggered_overlays`; checked by the same module.
- [ ] Negative control: with no project overlay, both trigger functions produce byte-identical results to current behavior — the pre-existing tests in `tests/unit/test_criteria_overlay.py` pass unmodified.
- [ ] Malformed project entries are ignored, not raised; checked by unit test.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `pytest tests/unit/test_criteria_overlay.py` all pass.
